title: AI-driven multi-omics integration in precision oncology: bridging the data deluge to clinical decisions

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《AI-driven multi-omics integration in precision oncology: bridging the data deluge to clinical decisions》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-1】Cancer's staggering molecular heterogeneity demands innovative approaches beyond traditional single-omics methods.

evidence.text: Cancer's staggering molecular heterogeneity demands innovative approaches beyond traditional single-omics methods.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《AI-driven multi-omics integration in precision oncology: bridging the data deluge to clinical decisions》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-7】Emerging trends, federated learning for privacy-preserving collaboration, spatial/single-cell omics for microenvironment decoding, quantum computing, and patient-centric "N-of-1" models, signal a paradigm shift toward dynamic, personalized cancer management.

evidence.text: Emerging trends, federated learning for privacy-preserving collaboration, spatial/single-cell omics for microenvironment decoding, quantum computing, and patient-centric "N-of-1" models, signal a paradigm shift toward dynamic, personalized cancer management.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《AI-driven multi-omics integration in precision oncology: bridging the data deluge to clinical decisions》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Abstract · abstract-1-2】The integration of multi-omics data, spanning genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics and radiomics, can improve diagnostic and prognostic accuracy when accompanied by rigorous preprocessing and external validation; for example, recent integrated classifiers report AUCs around 0.81-0.87 for difficult early-detection tasks.

evidence.text: The integration of multi-omics data, spanning genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics and radiomics, can improve diagnostic and prognostic accuracy when accompanied by rigorous preprocessing and external validation; for example, recent integrated classifiers report AUCs around 0.81-0.87 for difficult early-detection tasks.
